question: How do first-time workspace admins make sense of initial setup?

codebook.name: Unclear next step
codebook.definition: The participant describes not knowing which action the product expected of them next.

include.text: Says they did not know what to do next or where to go
Describes searching the interface for the next action

exclude.text: Knew the next step but could not take it for lack of access (use ACCESS)
General comment on design with no moment of not knowing

codebook.name: Waiting on access
codebook.definition: Setup pauses because the participant needs another person to grant a right or approval.

include.text: Names a person or team they had to wait for
Describes a request for rights, licences or approval

exclude.text: Has the rights but cannot find the setting (use NEXT)

codebook.name: Workaround
codebook.definition: The participant reaches the goal by a route the product did not offer for it.

include.text: Describes an improvised route, tool or manual step

exclude.text: Uses a documented feature as documented

codebook.name: Learning from a colleague
codebook.definition: The participant learns how setup works from another person rather than from the product.

include.text: Mentions asking, watching or copying a colleague

exclude.text: Contact with vendor support (not a colleague)

transcript.speaker: INT
transcript.text: Can you both walk me through the first hour after you created the workspace?

transcript.speaker: P1
transcript.text: The welcome screen was nice, but once it closed I was on an empty dashboard and I just did not know where to go. I clicked around the left menu for a while looking for something that said setup.

transcript.speaker: P2
transcript.text: For me it was the user import. I knew exactly where it was, the button was greyed out, and I had to wait two days for our IT team to give me the admin licence.

transcript.speaker: INT
transcript.text: What did you do in those two days?

transcript.speaker: P2
transcript.text: I kept a spreadsheet of everyone who needed an account and pasted the emails in one by one once the licence came through. There is a bulk upload somewhere but I never found it.

transcript.speaker: P1
transcript.text: Honestly the thing that unblocked me was sitting next to Dana from finance, who had set up her team the month before. I watched her do it and copied her settings.

transcript.speaker: INT
transcript.text: Did you look at the help centre at any point?

transcript.speaker: P1
transcript.text: I opened it once. The articles assume you already know what a space and a project are, so it did not help much at that stage.

transcript.speaker: P2
transcript.text: I raised a ticket with the vendor about the permissions page and they answered the same day, which was good.

transcript.speaker: P1
transcript.text: Looking back it all makes sense now. It is just that first hour.

annotations.span: I just did not know where to go

exclusions_considered.reason: There is a specific moment: the empty dashboard.

annotations.reasoning: P1 names the moment, after the welcome screen closed, and says in plain words they did not know where to go, then describes searching the menu.
annotations.counter_reading: This could be a general complaint about the empty dashboard design rather than a moment of not knowing.

annotations.span: I had to wait two days for our IT team to give me the admin licence

exclusions_considered.reason: P2 says they knew where the import was; the right was missing.

annotations.reasoning: P2 knew where the import was and could not use it until IT granted a licence, which names both the team and the rights request.
annotations.counter_reading: The greyed-out button might also mean the control was unclear, not only that access was missing.

annotations.span: I kept a spreadsheet of everyone who needed an account and pasted the emails in one by one

exclusions_considered.reason: P2 says they never found the bulk upload, so this is not the documented route.

annotations.reasoning: A spreadsheet and manual pasting is an improvised route to the goal of adding users while the bulk path stayed hidden.
annotations.counter_reading: Manual entry may be a documented option for small teams, in which case it is ordinary use.

annotations.span: I watched her do it and copied her settings

exclusions_considered.reason: Dana is a colleague in finance, not vendor support.

annotations.reasoning: P1 says a colleague's own setup unblocked them, and describes watching and copying it rather than learning from the product.
annotations.counter_reading: Copying settings could also be read as a workaround, since it bypasses whatever path the product offers.
